bayts.text: To you, O Best of creatures (Muḥammad), the greeting of peace of your servant, whom you have spared from blame.
May our Lord, the Peace (As-Salām), bless you forever, with a greeting of peace, together with the Family and the Companions.
You have attained a station beneath which is every station, O light of every worshipper who has fasted and kept vigil (in prayer).
You are the one through whom (Allah) brought us out of the darkness to the light of Him Who favoured you with the Word.
The Beautiful (Al-Jamīl) has given you glad tidings, O best of imāms, of what I have intended for you: an effort endowed with completeness.
You are the Prophet, the Messenger and the magnanimous; through you the righteous let themselves be led by the rein.
To you (is granted), with the Lord of creatures, every aspiration; to you, through Him, O my master, the most sublime reverence.
An Everlasting One, far exalted above sleep, has bestowed (His gifts) on us through you: for you are, my master, the best of mankind.
I have intended to thank Him for you every year and every month, and the Book (the Qurʾān) is a support for me.
I have intended to thank Him for you with the reed-pens and otherwise, O possessor of the all-comprehending word.
My gift, accept it out of generosity, without cease, O you who lead to me, from your God, my aspiration.
I have repented to my Lord, visiting you with this poem; and before it you bestowed (gifts) immense.
(The companions of the Garden:) they shall abide therein forever (Qurʾān 2:82).
My gift, from Muḥarram until Jumādā II, (is) fruits within easy reach.
Al-Māḥī (Muḥammad) has made me possess gifts that guard against every harm; from the best of Verses, (gifts) that suffice.
I have gladdened him with services that have no equal among services, (services) that are not fleeting.
My letters gladden my master, inviting to his Gardens and hastening toward them.
My gift to the Prophet is pure: glad tidings, bearing abundant good things.
Truly my reed-pens, through the Prophet, guide to the Gardens of Him Whose loftiness is manifest.
Service to the Best of the worlds drives out whoever hates me, and the dwellings stay empty of him.
Our Aḥmad (Muḥammad), of manifestly lofty rank, raises whoever loves him and makes whoever hates him vanish.
To Aḥmad, the Chosen, I have led the rhyme, (gaining) a well-being that endures, that does not fade.
The degree of the Chosen is not hidden, since (his) life is healing for the servants.
My love (goes) to my Lord and to him (the Prophet); for me (He) has softened, for me alone, what was hard: I am never, for all time, forgetful of it.
I have conversed intimately (with Him) in it (this poem), from Muḥarram until Jumādā II, (with) the Giver of fruits within easy reach.
